_partNote: Every class here is some kind of engine, so the tiles are kept apart by silhouette rather than by subject: a stubby wide-nacelle turbofan with a full fan face, a long thin empty duct with a nose spike, a big flared bell with a turbopump, a small flat-faced gridded ion thruster, a flat square solar sail, a squat ring-mouthed detonation can, and an unducted propeller on a disc motor. Class 5 uses the solar sail rather than a nuclear thermal engine because the nuclear engines would draw as another bell nozzle and collide with class 3, and every prompt asks for the hardware sitting still with no plume or flame.

partPrompts.1: A high-bypass turbofan engine sitting on a low stand, seen three-quarter: a short wide barrel-shaped nacelle, wider than it is long, whose circular front opening is almost entirely filled by a fan face of about twenty broad curved blades around a pointed spinner cone. A smooth outer casing wraps the nacelle and a short pylon stub sits on top. One bold object with a dominant circular fan face, no aircraft, no wing, no open propeller, no cutaway, no exhaust and no flame.
partPrompts.2: A ramjet duct lying horizontally on two low supports, seen three-quarter: a long slender tube of constant diameter with a sharp pointed conical centerbody spike projecting forward out of the circular inlet at one end and a plain open circular opening at the other. The duct is hollow and completely empty, with no fan blades, no compressor, no spinner and no propeller anywhere inside it. One long thin object, no flared bell, no nacelle, no plume.
partPrompts.3: A liquid rocket engine standing upright on a low stand, seen three-quarter: a large deeply flared bell nozzle with straight vertical tube-wall ribbing down its outside, narrowing to a domed combustion chamber at the top, with a small gimbal block above it and one compact cylindrical turbopump bolted to the side. The bell mouth is much wider than the throat and dominates the silhouette. No flame, no exhaust plume, no rocket body, no cutaway.
partPrompts.4: A gridded ion thruster standing on a small square mounting plate, seen three-quarter: a short squat body that flares outward like a truncated cone to a flat circular face at the front, that face covered by a coarse regular pattern of round holes. A raised rim runs around the edge of the face and one small tube-shaped cathode sits just outside it. Small and dish-like, not a flared bell nozzle, not an open-ended tube, no moving parts, no plume.
partPrompts.5: A square solar sail seen three-quarter: one large flat thin membrane stretched taut as a single square sheet, with four straight slender booms running out from a small box-shaped hub at the center to the four corners, and a few faint diagonal creases across the sheet. The flat square outline is the entire silhouette. No nozzle, no engine, no dish, no cylinder and no rocket hardware of any kind.
partPrompts.6: A rotating detonation engine combustor standing upright on a thick square mounting flange, seen three-quarter: a short thick-walled cylindrical can, open at the top, with a second solid cylinder standing concentrically inside it so the opening reads as a narrow ring-shaped gap between the two walls. A single row of small round injector ports runs around the outside of the can near the flange. Squat and heavy, not a flared bell, not a long slim duct, no flame and no exhaust.
partPrompts.7: An aircraft electric propulsion unit on a short stub mount, seen three-quarter: a shallow disc-shaped motor with radial cooling fins around its rim and a three-blade propeller of long slim blades bolted to its front face. Well separated behind it and clearly smaller lies a flat rectangular battery pack slab with a plain ribbed lid. The blades are long, thin and unducted, with no nacelle, no cowling, no ring around the blades and no fan face.
